purpose: Check whether a distributed reduction that returns only one rounded scalar per worker preserves cancellation information, compared with a worker state that carries both sum and compensation.

methods.scalar_partials: Each worker emits one float (naive, Kahan, Neumaier total, or math.fsum); worker partials are merged with adjacent pairwise summation.
methods.compensation_state: Each worker emits (sum, compensation); all components are merged using Neumaier compensated summation.

correctness_reference: sum(Fraction.from_float(x) for x in original input), rounded once to binary64
runtime_note: Deterministic simulation only. No real threads, GPU, distributed runtime, network transport, or production workload were executed.
reproducibility: The SHA-256-key permutation is explicitly defined so orderings are stable across Python versions.
cross_version_reproduction: The same frozen 330-case summary and case-matrix SHA-256 were reproduced on CPython 3.13.5 and CPython 3.14.4; this is not a cross-architecture test.
